claim: A complete alternate repair can preserve recoverable original widths using document-wide tag constraints while satisfying the same admissible historical/current/restart contract. Requiring exact equality with the official repair's widest-type outputs wrongly rejects this valid policy in the measured cases.
premise: The required producer property is one tag per dtype_name within one document. Explicit tags exclude that dtype as another bare tag's meaning. Numeric widths come from the declared pandas2.1.4 native numeric universe, not the benchmark's column names or numeric ranges. If document evidence is incomplete, retain the widest-type fallback.

insufficient_information_control.interpretation: The lone pd/f collision remains ambiguous and decodes conservatively to float64; current newly written float32/64 retain their explicit widths across a new process.

negative_control.interpretation: Program completion alone does not validate repair. Explicit width/value corruption is rejected despite successful load and resave.

revision_disclosure: Initial v1 passed all numerical checks but independent source review found all(empty) could misclassify an empty Interval-tag payload. V1 was retained. Separately frozen v2 adds nonempty kind-compatible payload evidence before inference, reruns84 checks, and tests genuine empty/nonempty Interval artifacts. This is author-developed resource calibration, not an unmodified preregistered agent result.
interval_scope: V2 matches the conservative reference on all three genuine Interval controls at initial and restart stages. Old/base and the backport already lose empty Interval type to float64; whole fixed restores Interval but with float64 subtype. We do not claim full Interval correctness or equality of the backport to every whole-fixed behavior.
distinction_from_upstream_comparator: The comparison here is naïve exact fixed-reader observation equality versus the declared admissible contract. It does not show that authentic upstream PR tests reject the valid alternate repair. The prior authentic-upstream comparison remains zero added rejections.
limits: One targeted numerical-code lineage, not60 independent defects or a prevalence estimate.
The alternate patches were written by the researchers, not generated by the main Gemma study.
The ambiguity was known upstream; this validates a reusable acceptance contract rather than claiming discovery of information loss.
No main model, data, oracle, framework or denominator was changed.

external_review.execution: Separate release-only CLI execution and patch application on the same physical Spark; not independent hardware.
external_review.supplemental_scope: Independent reviewer read the already executed Interval/collision controls; did not claim to independently rerun those supplemental controls.
